description: Test cases for the comment-review composition skill. Each eval exercises the 4-protocol pipeline (/inquire × /sublate × /gap × /contextualize + channel-loop) against a different artifact type + fixation event combination, verifying the caller-supplied signature (artifact_path, fixation_event D, application_context) routes scopes correctly and that the channel-loop augmentation activates for the terminal applicability check.

evals.name: blog-post-publish
evals.prompt: I've got a draft at ~/.claude/.write/2026-04-21-epistemic-protocols-composition.md for a Medium post about how epistemic protocols handle composition — I cite Ray Amjad's artifact framework and reference our own graph.json structure. Before I publish to medium.com and linkedin.com I want a full review: verify my factual claims (especially the Ray Amjad attribution and a couple of stats about LLM gate-response rates I pulled from a paper), audit for consideration gaps at the publish decision (counter-arguments, audience misfit, disclosure of AI-assisted writing), and then render it in a browser so I can leave inline comments on specific sentences. Walk me through it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the four protocols in scan-step order with D='publish' (stakes High — externally visible). Step 1: /inquire dispatches to CanonicalExternal for Ray Amjad source + paper cites, UserTacit for stats that lack web source. Step 2: /sublate audits the asserted sources per claim — the Ray Amjad framework as authority for the composition claim, the paper as authority for the gate-response stat — positing an antithesis against each and materializing an open verdict plus at most one instruction for next-round sidepanel disposition. Step 3: /gap surfaces consideration/audience/disclosure gaps. Phase 0 opens the channel BEFORE any sub-protocol runs — bun preflight, termination prose, bun scripts/serve.ts launch, browser preview, then the round-mode gate. Step 4: /contextualize scans the artifact against the application context. feedback-2026-04-21-epistemic-protocols-composition.jsonl accumulates comments for re-entry.

evals.name: plan-file-commit
evals.prompt: Before I start executing on ~/.claude/plans/anamnesis-stage3-hypomnesis-write.md I need a thorough review. The plan references current Anamnesis Phase 0 scan behavior, cites the canonical protocol registry in scripts/load-protocols.js for the set of protocols anamnesis feeds, and proposes a new SessionEnd hook schedule. I want to verify the factual references are still accurate (the protocol may have shifted since I drafted this), audit planning gaps (what could I be missing about rollback, what alternative implementation paths I haven't considered, what assumptions I'm carrying silently), and check that the plan actually fits the current worktree + merge-freeze context. Then I want to leave inline notes in the browser before I commit to executing any of this.
evals.expected_output: Runs with D='commit to execution', application_context='current worktree + merge freeze state'. Step 1: /inquire verifies the cited protocol registry via CodeDerivable (read scripts/load-protocols.js), verifies Anamnesis Phase 0 behavior via CodeDerivable (read anamnesis SKILL.md). Step 2: /sublate audits the plan's own cited sources per claim — the registry read as authority for the protocol set, the Anamnesis file read as authority for its Phase 0 behavior — tagging provenance/freshness/leverage and positing an antithesis against each. Step 3: /gap surfaces procedural/alternative/assumption gaps at the commit-to-execution decision with default stakes Medium — the caller signature tags commit-to-execution as Reversible, and Medium is that tag's default. Step 4: /contextualize scans Convention/Environment/Dependency against the plan. The channel was already opened at Phase 0, before Step 1.

evals.name: realign-direction-line
evals.prompt: I just ran /realign and the fused direction line plus per-horizon trace is staged in CLAUDE.md as a working diff. Before I commit and push the new line to main I want a full review: factual references in the trace (cited issue numbers, PR review excerpts, closed disposition trajectory entries) should match what's actually in the repository, consideration gaps at the direction-line commit (what if accumulated open issues since the trace shift the fusion the moment after I push? what rollback failure modes am I not anticipating?), and whether the fused line actually fits the categorization-axis use that downstream skills like /triage make of the project guide direction. I need to catch drift before it pollutes the next session's first-utterance baseline.
evals.expected_output: Runs with D='commit and push direction-line update', application_context='fresh-context next session reading the inscribed line as northstar'. Step 1: /inquire verifies factual claims via CodeDerivable (issue numbers via gh, PR review quotes via gh) + git log for closed-disposition trajectory consistency. Step 2: /sublate audits each cited source under the one claim it is read as authority for — the PR review quote for the disposition claim, the git log for the trajectory claim — freshness being the load-bearing tag where a direction line outlives the state it was read off. Step 3: /gap surfaces assumption/alternative gaps at the commit decision with High stakes (the line is read by every fresh session). Step 4: /contextualize scans for Convention (CLAUDE.md direction-line format) / Environment (open-issue landscape vs trace timestamp) / Dependency (downstream skills consuming the line as a categorization axis) mismatches; the channel was already opened at Phase 0, before Step 1.
